Assessment (adjusted with SLOOS)
- Policy tone: Moderately dovish and risk‑management oriented. The 50 bp cut to 4.75–5.00% and confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2% point to easing as labor slack edges up. Continuing QT and well‑calibrated implementation settings (IORB, SRF, ON RRP) help preserve anti‑inflation credibility.
- SLOOS overlay: The July 2024 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates credit supply remains a headwind. Banks reported tighter or still‑tight standards and weaker demand for C&I and CRE loans, with wider spreads and reduced risk appetite. Consumer credit (credit cards, auto, other) also saw tighter standards/terms and rising delinquency pressures, while residential real estate and HELOC standards were not broadly easing. These dynamics imply restrained credit creation and persistent stress in CRE—especially offices—consistent with the FSR’s flagged vulnerabilities.
- Net read: While the statement is credibly dovish and supportive for the outlook, SLOOS suggests bank‑intermediated credit remains restrictive, tempering the near‑term boost from policy easing. Maintain a cautiously positive stance but shade sentiment down from a pure macro read.
